comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C43-C46. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers found the genetic characterization and flow cytometry validation of the Ly49 knockout model to be well-supported. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the model as a 'precise deletion' and OpenEval confirmed support from sequencing and flow cytometry data.

Disagreement on claims C47-C48 regarding NKG2A expression. OpenEval found these claims supported by flow cytometry data, but peer Reviewer 3 expressed uncertainty and requested clarification about NKG2A's role and influence of other inhibitory receptors. OpenEval evaluated C47-C52 together as supported, while peer review only questioned C47-C48.

Disagreement on claim C51 (KLRG1 reduction). OpenEval found C51 supported as part of comprehensive flow cytometry data (C47-C52), but peer Reviewer 3 expressed uncertainty about whether KLRG1 expression changes are due to Ly49 receptor loss or chromosomal manipulations, requesting clarification of the mechanism.

Disagreement on claim C52 (NK cell maturation). OpenEval found C52 supported within the broader set C47-C52, but peer Reviewer 3 noted an inconsistency between the Figure 1 title (stating less mature phenotype) and Results text (stating no difference in maturation), flagging this for clarification.

Agreement on claims C53 and C4 regarding licensing defects. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers found the evidence for loss of NK cell licensing convincing, with reduced IFN-gamma production demonstrated by flow cytometry. OpenEval evaluated a broader set (C3-C4, C53-C55, C59-C60) while peer review focused on C53 and C4.

Agreement on claims C54-C55 regarding intact effector machinery. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accepted the PMA/ionomycin control experiment as demonstrating that functional defects are specific to licensing rather than general impairment. OpenEval included these in a broader evaluation while peer review treated them separately.

Agreement on claims C3, C59-C60 regarding loss of missing-self recognition. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers found the in vivo rejection assay data convincing. OpenEval evaluated these with additional claims (C4, C53-C55) while peer review grouped them with C56-C58, C61 as part of the missing-self rejection findings.

Agreement on claims C56-C58, C61 regarding differential MHC-I allele recognition. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accepted the in vivo cytotoxicity data showing differential rejection of targets lacking different MHC-I alleles. OpenEval also included C87-C88 in this evaluation while peer review grouped these claims with C3, C59-C60.

Agreement on claims C87-C88 regarding H-2Kb importance. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accepted the finding that H-2Kb is more important for missing-self recognition than H-2Db. OpenEval grouped these with C56-C58, C61 while peer review also included C89-C90 in their evaluation.

Agreement on claims C62-C65 regarding Ly49A expression in the knock-in model. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers found the flow cytometry data showing correlation between NKp46 and Ly49A expression to be well-supported. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly praised the re-introduction approach. OpenEval also included C102 in this evaluation.

Agreement on claim C102 regarding lower Ly49A expression levels. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accepted that Ly49A expression from the Ncr1 locus shows lower MFI than wildtype. OpenEval grouped this with C62-C65 while peer review connected it to functional competence claims C103-C104.

Agreement on claims C66-C67 regarding NK cell maturation. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers found the maturation analysis showing similar percentages of mature NK cells across genotypes to be supported. OpenEval also included C85-C86 in this evaluation while peer review treated maturation findings separately.

Agreement on claims C85-C86 regarding Ly49 receptors not affecting NK cell development. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accepted this conclusion based on maturation data. OpenEval grouped these with C66-C67 while peer review treated them as a separate finding about development versus licensing/recognition.

Initial disagreement resolved on claim C5 regarding KLRG1 regulation. OpenEval found C5 supported by the rescue experiment, while peer Reviewer 3 initially expressed uncertainty about chromosomal regulatory elements. However, the reviewer later stated 'The authors have successfully answered all my questions,' indicating resolution.

Agreement on claims C68-C69, C8, C95-C96 regarding KLRG1 rescue. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers found the rescue experiment compelling, with Ly49A expressed from chromosome 7 restoring KLRG1 and arguing against cis-regulatory effects. Peer review noted initial concerns were resolved by this experiment. OpenEval also included C5 in this evaluation.

Perfect agreement on claims C70-C74, C77, C7, C82 regarding licensing rescue. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers found the functional rescue data (IFN-gamma production and degranulation) strongly convincing. Peer reviewers called it 'a novel and important finding' with 'solid' evidence, matching OpenEval's strong support assessment.

Strong agreement on claims C78-C81, C6, C9, C83, C105 regarding sufficiency of single Ly49 receptor. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers strongly endorsed this central finding, with peer reviewers calling it 'novel and important' and the editor noting it provides 'valuable insights.' OpenEval also included C103 in this evaluation.

Agreement on claim C103 regarding functional competence despite lower expression. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accepted that Ly49A KI cells are fully functional despite lower expression levels. OpenEval grouped this with the sufficiency claims (C78-C81, C6, C9, C83, C105) while peer review connected it to expression level observations (C102, C104).

Agreement on claims C89-C90 regarding MHC-I binding specificity. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accepted the interpretation about differential Ly49 receptor binding to MHC-I alleles. OpenEval noted the caveat about overexpression systems in cited studies, while peer reviewers accepted the findings without critique.

Perfect agreement on claims C75-C76 regarding intact effector machinery. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accepted the PMA/ionomycin control as demonstrating that functional defects are specific to receptor-mediated activation rather than general impairment. Both treated this as an important control experiment.

Agreement on claim C104 regarding expression level thresholds. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accepted the inference that expression level thresholds are not limiting for licensing function. OpenEval noted this conclusion is context-limited, while peer reviewers accepted it as evidence of model robustness.

OpenEval identified claims C94 and C98 as uncertain/speculative statements about regulatory elements and licensing-KLRG1 mechanisms that require further investigation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressed these speculative claims, though peer Reviewer 3's concerns about regulatory elements (addressed in R3/R10) are related.

OpenEval evaluated claims C49-C50, C101 regarding heterozygous deletion effects on Ly49 expression as supported, noting interesting observations about stochastic expression mechanisms. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressed these claims about gene dosage effects.

OpenEval evaluated claims C1-C2, C10-C29 as background knowledge supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation addressed these background claims, as peer reviewers focused on novel experimental findings rather than contextual literature.

OpenEval evaluated claims C30-C42 describing prior work as accurately cited and providing rationale for the study. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressed these claims about previous studies, as peer reviewers focused on the current experimental results.

OpenEval evaluated claim C84 as a citation to prior work (Zhang 2019) appropriately qualifying conclusions about Ly49 sufficiency. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressed this citation or qualification.

OpenEval evaluated claims C91-C93, C97, C99-C100 as background knowledge supported by appropriate citations providing context for KLRG1 and Ly49 expression data. No corresponding peer review evaluation addressed these background claims.
